title: Replay Codex native task proposal review

requirement.summary: Run one fresh event-level Codex replay against installed Adapter 1.3.0, route the native proposal form to the current human chat, and retain only normalized outcomes.

objective.rationale: Source behavior and installed-runtime preflight pass, but no fresh production-host replay has yet shown Codex materialization, native elicitation, and an exact human-bound outcome together.

goal: Prove one fresh Codex App Server journey can turn an ordinary bounded request into the installed Adapter 1.3.0 proposal-review form, return the exact choice through the current chat, and finish without unauthorized implementation or retained raw material.
non_goals: Do not implement the proposed task, modify AgentGov source or configuration, replace the installed runtime, add another host, or run a second replay.
Do not retain the raw request, transcript, Agent messages, reasoning, command output, source content, credentials, absolute paths, or unbounded MCP payloads.
Do not treat tool permission as task admission or grant implementation, scope expansion, exception, Git, publication, release, deployment, or consumer authority.
Do not touch NYC or another project, install dependencies, create another environment, or claim semantic fidelity beyond the observed bounded journey.
acceptance_signals: A fresh ephemeral Codex App Server thread loads the project configuration and installed Adapter 1.3.0 with the capability-gated proposal-review tool.
An ordinary bounded work request causes one completed agentgov_task_proposal_review journey and one native form is surfaced to the product owner through the current chat.
The exact human choice is bound to that form; only admit may exclusively create the displayed task, while change, reject, cancellation, malformed input, or interruption writes no task.
The bridge retains only normalized form, decision, tool-result, and terminal-status fields and removes all transient files after evidence extraction.
Task, scope, repository, documentation, and diff checks pass or report only explicitly preserved pre-existing exclusions; no proposed implementation begins.

items: The fresh Codex process transmits repository instructions and context to the OpenAI service under the product owner's explicit approval.
A bridge bug could retain raw host output or bind the wrong decision unless it parses only exact protocol events and request identity.
Admit creates one new task file even though it grants no implementation authority; every other outcome must remain zero-write.
A host, schema, installed-runtime, or protocol mismatch could interrupt the replay and must remain fail-closed.

stop_conditions: Stop if the fresh process does not load installed Adapter 1.3.0 and the capability-gated proposal-review tool through the existing project configuration.
Stop if a normalized form cannot be routed to the current chat or its exact request identity cannot be preserved for the response.
Stop before any proposed implementation, source/config/install change, second replay, additional external transmission, Git write, publication, release, deployment, or consumer mutation.
Stop on raw-material retention, unbounded diagnostics, unexpected repository write, stale plan, target race, or any required governance failure.

decision.rationale: The newly approved bridge passed local initialization and thread probes, then the real replay reached starting_turn before App Server closed without a turn response, form, tool call, or error code. Read-only follow-up found the standalone Codex CLI not logged in and no inheritable Codex/OpenAI credential environment variable. The authorization is consumed; authentication repair and another replay are not admitted.
